title: Context Management
description: Keep Claude's working memory clean, focused, and affordable.

lessons.title: The Context Window
lessons.description: Why long sessions get worse over time.

theory.title: Claude's desk has limited space
theory.body:
Everything in a session (your messages, Claude's replies, files it read, command output) piles into the **context window**. It's big, but finite.

As a session runs long, old and irrelevant content **crowds out** what matters now. Claude may lose track of earlier decisions or get distracted by stale details, and every turn costs more tokens.

Kip's rule: a tidy shell is a fast shell.

exercises.prompt: Why does a very long session tend to degrade?
options: Claude gets tired
Irrelevant earlier content crowds the limited context window
The terminal runs out of scrollback
Your API key slowly expires
exercises.explanation: Stale content competes for attention and space in the context window.

exercises.prompt: Which of these consume context?
exercises.explanation: Everything Claude sees during a session takes up room in its context window.

exercises.prompt: Two hours into a session, Claude starts mixing up details from an earlier, unrelated task. What's the likely cause?
options: A bug in your code
Old, unrelated context still in the conversation
Your CLAUDE.md is too short
The network is slow
exercises.explanation: Leftovers from a previous task can confuse the current one.

exercises.prompt: You only need Claude to check one failing test. Which request is more context-friendly?
options: Run the entire test suite with verbose logging and show me everything.
Run only the failing test in src/cart/total.test.ts and summarize why it fails.
exercises.explanation: Targeted commands keep huge, irrelevant output out of the context window.

exercises.prompt: Order how a session typically drifts.
steps: Session starts focused on one task
You add an unrelated side task
Lots of logs and files pile up
exercises.explanation: Mixing tasks and piling up output is how context quality slowly erodes.

exercises.prompt: Check how full your context window is right now.
exercises.hint: The command shares its name with the thing you're inspecting.
exercises.explanation: /context visualizes how your context window is being used.

theory.title: Wipe the whiteboard
theory.body:
`/clear` **wipes the conversation history** so you start with an empty context, while staying in the same session and project. Your `CLAUDE.md` still loads, so Claude keeps its project briefing.

Make it a habit: **finished a task? `/clear` before the next one.** Unrelated history only gets in the way.
theory.code:
> (bug fixed and committed)
> /clear
> Now add a CSV export to @src/reports/

exercises.prompt: You just finished a bug fix. Wipe the conversation before starting an unrelated feature.
exercises.explanation: /clear empties the conversation history so the next task starts clean.

exercises.prompt: After /clear, what does Claude still know about your project?
options: Nothing at all, ever again
Everything from the cleared conversation
What's in CLAUDE.md, plus whatever it reads anew
Only the last message
exercises.explanation: The conversation is gone, but memory files still give Claude its project briefing.

exercises.prompt: When is /clear the WRONG move?
options: Between two unrelated tasks
Mid-task, when Claude still needs details from this conversation
After committing a finished feature
When Claude is confused by old context
exercises.explanation: Clearing mid-task throws away context you still need; consider /compact instead.

exercises.prompt: Order a clean task-by-task workflow.
steps: Describe task A and let Claude implement it
Describe task B with full context in the prompt
exercises.explanation: Finishing, committing, then clearing keeps each task in a focused conversation.

exercises.prompt: You ran /clear and now want to continue a refactor you planned earlier. Which prompt works?
options: Continue the refactor we discussed.
Refactor @src/api/client.ts to use the fetch wrapper in @src/lib/http.ts; keep the exported function names unchanged.
exercises.explanation: After /clear Claude has no memory of the earlier chat, so the prompt must stand on its own.

exercises.prompt: Match the situation to the move.
exercises.explanation: Clear for new tasks, compact to keep going, continue to come back later.

exercises.prompt: Complete the habit.
exercises.code: Finished a task? Commit it, then run /___ before the next one.
exercises.explanation: /clear between tasks keeps each conversation focused.

theory.title: Keep the gist, drop the bulk
theory.body:
`/compact` **summarizes the conversation** so far and replaces the history with that summary, freeing up context while keeping the important bits.

Give it focus instructions to steer what's kept: `/compact keep the API design decisions and the failing test list`.

Claude Code also **auto-compacts** when you get close to the context limit, but compacting yourself at a natural breakpoint gives you control over what survives.
theory.code: > /compact focus on the database schema decisions

exercises.prompt: Summarize the conversation to free up context while staying on the same task.
exercises.explanation: /compact replaces the history with a summary so you can keep working with more room.

exercises.prompt: Compact the conversation with the focus instruction: focus on the auth flow decisions
accepted: /compact focus on the auth flow decisions
exercises.hint: Add your instructions after the command.
exercises.explanation: Text after /compact tells Claude what to prioritize in the summary.

exercises.prompt: What's the key difference between /clear and /compact?
options: /clear keeps a summary, /compact deletes everything
/compact keeps a summary of the history, /clear removes it
They're identical
/compact exits the session
exercises.explanation: /compact preserves the gist for continued work, while /clear starts from an empty conversation.

exercises.prompt: What happens if you never compact and the context approaches its limit?
options: The session crashes and is lost
Claude Code auto-compacts the conversation
Claude stops responding forever
Old messages are emailed to you
exercises.explanation: Auto-compact kicks in near the limit, but manual compaction lets you choose what's kept.

exercises.prompt: Steer the summary.
exercises.code: > /___ keep the list of ___ tests and the chosen fix
exercises.explanation: Focus instructions after /compact protect the details you still need.

exercises.prompt: Order a smart mid-task compaction.
steps: Notice the session is long but the task isn't done
Reach a natural checkpoint, like tests passing
Continue the task with freed-up context
exercises.explanation: Compacting at a checkpoint with focus keeps what matters and drops the noise.

exercises.prompt: You're mid-migration and context is getting heavy. Which command keeps the most useful information?
options: /compact
/compact keep the migration plan, completed steps, and remaining TODOs
exercises.explanation: Specific focus instructions make sure the summary keeps the plan and progress.

theory.title: Look at the gauges
theory.body:
`/context` shows a **visual breakdown** of what's filling your context window: system prompt, tools, memory files, messages.

`/cost` shows **token usage and cost** for the current session (most relevant for API users).

`/usage` shows your **plan's usage limits** if you're on a subscription.

Check the gauges before a big task, not after you've hit the wall.

exercises.prompt: You're paying per token through the API. Check this session's token usage and cost.
exercises.explanation: /cost reports token usage and cost for the current session.

exercises.prompt: You're on a subscription plan. Check your plan's usage limits.
exercises.explanation: /usage shows plan usage limits for subscribers.

exercises.prompt: Match the command to what it shows.
exercises.explanation: Three gauges and one action: look, then act.

exercises.prompt: /context shows your memory files take a surprising share of the window. What's a good fix?
options: Delete Claude Code
Trim CLAUDE.md to high-signal lines and use imports wisely
Run /cost repeatedly
Paste the files into chat instead
exercises.explanation: Memory loads every session, so a lean CLAUDE.md saves context everywhere.

exercises.prompt: Which habit reduces token usage the most over a day?
options: One giant session for every task
/clear between unrelated tasks and precise prompts
Asking Claude to repeat its answers
Running verbose logs for every command
exercises.explanation: Smaller, focused conversations mean every turn sends less history.

exercises.prompt: Order a context check before a big refactor.
steps: Run /context to see how full the window is
Decide whether earlier history still matters
Start the refactor with a focused prompt
exercises.explanation: Checking first lets you start big work with plenty of room.

exercises.scenario: You just ran /clear after finishing a bug fix. Next task: add rate limiting to the login endpoint. Write a self-contained prompt, since Claude no longer has the earlier conversation.
exercises.sample: Add rate limiting to POST /login in @src/routes/auth.ts using the existing middleware in @src/middleware/rateLimit.ts: max 5 attempts per IP per 15 minutes, returning 429 with a Retry-After header. Don't change other routes. Add tests; done when npm test passes.
exercises.explanation: A fresh context needs a self-contained prompt with files, limits, and a definition of done.

exercises.prompt: Pick the right gauge for each question.
exercises.code:
> /___    # What's in my context window?
> /___    # What has this session cost?
exercises.explanation: /context shows window usage while /cost shows session spend.

mission.title: Context Keeper
mission.intro: Run a real session with deliberate context hygiene and watch the gauges move.
checklist: Start a session, do a small task, then run /context and note how full it is
Run /compact with a focus instruction and check /context again
Commit your work, run /clear, and start an unrelated task with a self-contained prompt
Check /cost (API) or /usage (subscription) at the end of the session
mission.explanation: Clearing between tasks and compacting with focus keeps Claude sharp and your usage low.

cheatsheet.description: Everything Claude sees this session; finite, so keep it relevant.
Wipe conversation history; start the next task fresh.
Summarize history to free context and keep working.
Tell the summary what to keep.
Happens automatically near the context limit.
Visualize what's using your context window.
Show token usage and cost for this session.
Show plan usage limits for subscribers.
Clear between unrelated tasks to avoid drift.
